subject: Civil Engineering
title: Monitoring Slope Movement
description: A quick, practical guide to Monitoring Slope Movement.

hook.text: A slope can creep for months before it suddenly lets go. Sensors give early warning.

buildup.text: Inclinometers in boreholes track how deep soil layers shift over time.

discovery.text: GPS stations on the ground surface detect millimeter-scale movement from space.

twist.text: InSAR satellite radar can monitor entire mountainsides at once — no ground equipment.

climax.text: Norway's early warning system evacuated a village hours before a rockslide hit.

punchline.text: Measure the creep and you can predict the collapse.

quiz.question: What does an inclinometer measure in slope monitoring?
options: The temperature of the soil at various depths
The lateral movement of soil layers at different depths over time
The water content of the slope surface after rainfall
